records.source: וַיִּמְעֲל֧וּ בְנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל מַ֖עַל בַּחֵ֑רֶם וַיִּקַּ֡ח עָכָ֣ן בֶּן־כַּרְמִי֩ בֶן־זַבְדִּ֨י בֶן־זֶ֜רַח לְמַטֵּ֤ה יְהוּדָה֙ מִן־הַחֵ֔רֶם וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֥ף יְהוָ֖ה בִּבְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And acted unfaithfully [the] sons of Israel unfaithfulness in the devoted thing; and took Achan son of Carmi son of Zabdi son of Zerah, of [the] tribe of Judah, from the devoted thing, and burned [the] anger of Yahweh against [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: But the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} broke faith over the devoted things. Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, took a share of the devoted things, and the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.1: But the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel committed a breach of faith in the devoted things; for Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took from the devoted things, and the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.1: But the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} were unfaithful about the devoted things, the things that belonged to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} alone. A man named Achan took some of them. He was the son of Carmi and grandson of Zabdi, from the family line of Zerah in the tribe of Judah. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} became very angry with the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: broke faith: a breach of trust against what belonged to the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb and its noun are used together here ("acted unfaithfully with unfaithfulness"). The word means betraying a trust, and is used above all for taking or misusing what is holy and belongs to the LORD (Leviticus 5:15; 1 Chronicles 2:7 uses it of this same act).

decisions.choice: the devoted things: the goods of Jericho given over wholly to the LORD
decisions.reason: At Jericho everything was declared devoted to the LORD: the people were to be destroyed, and the silver, gold, bronze and iron were to go into the LORD's treasury (6:17-19). Such things could not be kept for private use (Leviticus 27:28). The singular noun names the whole body of devoted goods.

decisions.choice: one man's act counts as the act of all Israel
decisions.reason: Only Achan took the goods, yet the verse says "the sons of Israel" broke faith, and the LORD's anger burns against the whole people. Joshua had warned that taking devoted things would make the camp itself devoted and bring trouble on it (6:18). The rest of the chapter works this out.

decisions.choice: son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah: a line of descent, not three generations only
decisions.reason: Zerah was a son of Judah (Genesis 38:30), so "son of Zerah" means a descendant several generations down. The list fixes Achan's place in tribe, clan and family, the same steps the lot follows in verses 16-18. 1 Chronicles 2:6-7 gives the grandfather's name as Zimri and Achan's as Achar.

decisions.choice: the devoted things, the things that belonged to the LORD alone
decisions.reason: Readable explains "devoted things" the first time it appears in the chapter, in line with m2, and keeps the term itself as the other levels do.

decisions.choice: grandson of Zabdi, from the family line of Zerah
decisions.reason: Readable shows what each "son of" means in this list (m4), so young readers do not take Zerah to be Achan's great-grandfather.

records.heading: Breaking faith over the devoted things

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ אֲנָשִׁ֜ים מִֽירִיח֗וֹ הָעַ֞י אֲשֶׁ֨ר עִם־בֵּ֥ית אָ֨וֶן֙ מִקֶּ֣דֶם לְבֵֽית־אֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר עֲל֖וּ וְרַגְּל֣וּ אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַֽיַּעֲלוּ֙ הָאֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַֽיְרַגְּל֖וּ אֶת־הָעָֽי׃
records.gloss: And sent Joshua men from Jericho [to] Ai, which [is] beside Beth-aven, east of Bethel, and said to them, saying, Go up and spy out the land. And went up the men and spied out Ai.
pieces: Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which lies near Beth-aven, east of Bethel. He told them, "Go up and scout the land." So the men went up and scouted out Ai.

L.2: And Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which [is] near Beth-aven, east of Bethel, and spoke to them, saying, "Go up and spy out the land." And the men went up and spied out Ai.

R.2: Joshua sent some men from Jericho to the town of Ai. It was near Beth-aven, to the east of Bethel. He told them, "Go up and look over the land." So the men went up and checked out Ai.

decisions.choice: Ai, Beth-aven, Bethel: places in the hill country west of Jericho
decisions.reason: Ai means "the ruin" or "the heap" and always has the article in Hebrew. Bethel ("house of God") is the town where Jacob saw the ladder (Genesis 28:19), and Ai lay east of it (Genesis 12:8). Beth-aven ("house of trouble" or "house of wickedness") was a place nearby (18:12); Hosea later uses the name for Bethel itself in scorn (Hosea 4:15).

decisions.choice: go up and spy out: climb into the hills to scout the land
decisions.reason: Jericho lies low in the Jordan valley and Ai high in the hills, so the road "goes up". The word for the spies sent to Jericho comes from the same verb (2:1; 6:22).

decisions.choice: look over / checked out
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for scouting a place, which is what "spy out" means here.

records.source: וַיָּשֻׁ֣בוּ אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֗עַ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָיו֮ אַל־יַ֣עַל כָּל־הָעָם֒ כְּאַלְפַּ֣יִם אִ֗ישׁ א֚וֹ כִּשְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֣ים אִ֔ישׁ יַעֲל֖וּ וְיַכּ֣וּ אֶת־הָעָ֑י אַל־תְּיַגַּע־שָׁ֨מָּה֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָעָ֔ם כִּ֥י מְעַ֖ט הֵֽמָּה׃
records.gloss: And they returned to Joshua and said to him, Let not go up all the people; about two thousand men or about three thousand men let go up and let them strike Ai; do not make weary there all the people, for few [are] they.
pieces: They came back to Joshua and said to him, "There is no need for all the people to go up. Let about 2,000 or 3,000 men go up and attack Ai. Do not wear out the whole army with the climb, because the people of Ai are few."

L.3: And they returned to Joshua and said to him, "Do not let all the people go up; let about 2,000 men or about 3,000 men go up and strike Ai. Do not make all the people toil up there, for they are few."

R.3: When they came back to Joshua, they said, "Not everyone needs to go. Send about 2,000 or 3,000 men to attack Ai. Do not make the whole army climb up there. There are only a few people in Ai."

decisions.choice: do not make weary: do not tire out the whole army with the march up
decisions.reason: The verb means to make someone toil until tired. The climb from Jericho to Ai was long and steep, and the spies think the effort of moving the whole army is not worth it.

decisions.choice: they are few: the men of Ai
decisions.reason: "They" refers to the defenders of Ai, not to Israel's army. Verse 5 shows how wrong this confidence was.

decisions.choice: the whole army
decisions.reason: "All the people" here means the fighting men of Israel, so Balanced and Readable say "army" in the second clause, where the point is the march.

decisions.choice: the people of Ai
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who "they" are, as m2 explains.

records.source: וַיַּעֲל֤וּ מִן־הָעָם֙ שָׁ֔מָּה כִּשְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֖ים אִ֑ישׁ וַיָּנֻ֕סוּ לִפְנֵ֖י אַנְשֵׁ֥י הָעָֽי׃
records.gloss: And went up from the people there about three thousand men; and they fled before [the] men of Ai.
pieces: So about 3,000 of the people went up there, but they ran away from the men of Ai.

L.4: So about 3,000 men from the people went up there; and they fled before the men of Ai.

R.4: So about 3,000 men went up. But they ran away from the men of Ai.

decisions.choice: fled: the attack broke down at once
decisions.reason: The verse sets the two verbs side by side with no fighting between them: they went up, and they fled. The writer gives no account of a battle, only of a rout.

records.source: וַיַּכּ֨וּ מֵהֶ֜ם אַנְשֵׁ֣י הָעַ֗י כִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וְשִׁשָּׁה֙ אִ֔ישׁ וַֽיִּרְדְּפ֞וּם לִפְנֵ֤י הַשַּׁ֨עַר֙ עַד־הַשְּׁבָרִ֔ים וַיַּכּ֖וּם בַּמּוֹרָ֑ד וַיִּמַּ֥ס לְבַב־הָעָ֖ם וַיְהִ֥י לְמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And struck from them [the] men of Ai about thirty and six man, and pursued them before the gate as far as the Shebarim, and struck them on the descent; and melted [the] heart of the people and became water.
pieces: The men of Ai killed about thirty-six of them. They chased them from outside the city gate as far as Shebarim and struck them down on the slope. The people lost heart; their courage melted like water.

L.5: And the men of Ai struck down about thirty-six men of them, and chased them from before the gate as far as Shebarim, and struck them down on the descent. And the heart of the people melted and became water.

R.5: The men of Ai killed about thirty-six Israelites. They chased the rest from the city gate all the way to Shebarim and killed them on the way down the hill. Then the people of Israel were terrified. All their courage was gone.

decisions.choice: Shebarim: a place name, perhaps "the quarries" or "the breaks"
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning "break" and has the article, so it may describe a place of broken rock, such as quarries or ravines, east of Ai. It is not found elsewhere, and its site is unknown.

decisions.choice: the descent: the slope going down from Ai toward the Jordan valley
decisions.reason: The word means a downward road or slope. Israel was cut down while running downhill, back the way they had come.

decisions.choice: the heart melted and became water: they lost all courage
decisions.reason: The same picture is used of the Canaanites when they heard what the LORD had done for Israel (2:11; 5:1). Now it is Israel whose courage melts away: the roles are reversed.

decisions.choice: The people lost heart; their courage melted like water
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of melting and water and makes plain that it is about courage.

decisions.choice: Israelites / the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable names Israel, so that it is clear who was killed and who lost heart.

records.source: וַיִּקְרַ֨ע יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ שִׂמְלֹתָ֗יו וַיִּפֹּל֩ עַל־פָּנָ֨יו אַ֜רְצָה לִפְנֵ֨י אֲר֤וֹן יְהוָה֙ עַד־הָעֶ֔רֶב ה֖וּא וְזִקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיַּעֲל֥וּ עָפָ֖ר עַל־רֹאשָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And tore Joshua his clothes and fell on his face to [the] ground before [the] ark of Yahweh until the evening, he and [the] elders of Israel, and they put dust on their head.
pieces: Joshua tore his clothes and fell face down on the ground before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and he stayed there until evening, he and the elders of Israel. They threw dust on their heads.

L.6: And Joshua tore his clothes and fell on his face to the ground before the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} until the evening, he and the elders of Israel; and they put dust on their heads.

R.6: Joshua tore his clothes to show his sorrow. He lay face down on the ground in front of the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} until evening. The leaders of Israel did the same, and they threw dust on their heads.

decisions.choice: tearing clothes and putting dust on the head: signs of grief and mourning
decisions.reason: People tore their clothes and put dust or ashes on their heads when they mourned the dead or faced disaster (Genesis 37:34; 1 Samuel 4:12; 2 Samuel 1:2). Joshua and the elders mourn and humble themselves before God.

decisions.choice: before the ark of the LORD: in the place where the LORD was present among his people
decisions.reason: The ark was the sign of the LORD's presence that had gone before Israel across the Jordan and around Jericho (3:11; 6:4). To fall down before it is to bring the disaster to God himself.

decisions.choice: to show his sorrow
decisions.reason: Readable adds the meaning of the gesture (m1), which modern readers may not know.

decisions.choice: The leaders of Israel
decisions.reason: "Elders" were the senior men who led the tribes. Readable uses "leaders", the plainer word.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ אֲהָ֣הּ׀אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה לָ֠מָה הֵעֲבַ֨רְתָּ הַעֲבִ֜יר אֶת־הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן לָתֵ֥ת אֹתָ֛נוּ בְּיַ֥ד הָאֱמֹרִ֖י לְהַאֲבִידֵ֑נוּ וְלוּ֙ הוֹאַ֣לְנוּ וַנֵּ֔שֶׁב בְּעֵ֖בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And said Joshua, Alas, Lord Yahweh, why have you surely brought over this people over the Jordan to give us into [the] hand of the Amorite to destroy us? And if only we had been content and stayed beyond the Jordan!
pieces: Then Joshua said, "Oh, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, why did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} ever bring this people across the Jordan, only to hand us over to the Amorites to destroy us? If only we had been willing to stay on the other side of the Jordan!

L.7: And Joshua said, "Alas, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}! Why did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring this people over the Jordan at all, to give us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us? If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan!

R.7: Joshua said, "Oh, {{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, why did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bring these people across the Jordan River? Was it only to hand us over to the Amorites so they could destroy us? We should have been happy to stay on the other side of the Jordan!

decisions.choice: why did you bring ... at all: a strong, grieving complaint
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis ("bringing over, have you brought over"). Joshua does not doubt that God brought Israel across; he asks why God did it if this was to be the result. His words echo Israel's complaints in the wilderness (Exodus 14:11; Numbers 14:2-3).

decisions.choice: the Amorites: the peoples of the hill country of Canaan
decisions.reason: "Amorite" is often used for the people of Canaan as a whole, especially those in the hills (Genesis 15:16; Deuteronomy 1:7). Here it includes the men of Ai.

decisions.choice: if only we had been content: a wish about the past
decisions.reason: The verb means to be willing or to settle for something. Joshua wishes Israel had settled for the land east of the Jordan, where two and a half tribes had already taken their share (1:12-15).

decisions.choice: Lord GOD
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "my Lord" followed by the divine name. The settled rendering is "Lord GOD" (or "Lord Yahweh" by the reader's setting), so that "Lord" is not written twice.

decisions.choice: Was it only to hand us over ...?
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long question into two short ones, keeping its sense of protest.

records.source: בִּ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י מָ֣ה אֹמַ֔ר אַ֠חֲרֵי אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָפַ֧ךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עֹ֖רֶף לִפְנֵ֥י אֹיְבָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Please, my Lord, what will I say after that has turned Israel [the] back before its enemies?
pieces: Please, Lord, what can I say now that Israel has turned and run from its enemies?

L.8: Please, Lord, what can I say, now that Israel has turned [its] back before its enemies?

R.8: Lord, what can I say? Israel has turned and run away from its enemies!

decisions.choice: please, my Lord: a humble opening to a plea
decisions.reason: The first word is used to ask leave to speak to a superior (Genesis 44:18; Exodus 4:10). "My Lord" here is a title of respect addressed to God, without the divine name.

decisions.choice: turned the back: fled in defeat
decisions.reason: To "turn the neck" (that is, the back of the neck) to an enemy is to run away from him. Israel had been promised that no one would stand against it (1:5).

decisions.choice: Lord, what can I say?
decisions.reason: Readable leaves the polite "please" unspoken and lets "Lord" carry the address; the humble tone is kept by the question.

records.source: וְיִשְׁמְע֣וּ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֗י וְכֹל֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ וְנָסַ֣בּוּ עָלֵ֔ינוּ וְהִכְרִ֥יתוּ אֶת־שְׁמֵ֖נוּ מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ וּמַֽה־תַּעֲשֵׂ֖ה לְשִׁמְךָ֥ הַגָּדֽוֹל׃ס
records.gloss: And will hear the Canaanite and all [the] inhabitants of the land, and they will surround us and cut off our name from the earth; and what will you do for your great name?
pieces: The Canaanites and everyone who lives in the land will hear of it. They will surround us and wipe our name off the earth. Then what will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great name?"

L.9: And the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear [of it], and they will surround us and cut off our name from the earth; and what will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great name?"

R.9: The Canaanites and all the other people in the land will hear about this. They will surround us and wipe us out, and no one will even remember us. Then what will happen to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great name?"

decisions.choice: cut off our name from the earth: destroy us so that no memory of us remains
decisions.reason: A person's or people's "name" lives on in their descendants and in memory. To have it cut off is to be wiped out completely (Deuteronomy 7:24; 1 Samuel 24:22).

decisions.choice: your great name: the LORD's reputation among the nations
decisions.reason: Joshua's final plea is not only for Israel. If Israel is destroyed, the nations will think the LORD could not keep his promises, as Moses argued before (Exodus 32:12; Numbers 14:13-16; Deuteronomy 9:28).

decisions.choice: what will happen to your great name?
decisions.reason: Readable puts the question in terms of what becomes of God's name, which is the point of "what will you do for your great name" (m2).

records.source: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ קֻ֣ם לָ֑ךְ לָ֣מָּה זֶּ֔ה אַתָּ֖ה נֹפֵ֥ל עַל־פָּנֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Joshua, Stand up for yourself; why [is] this [that] you [are] falling on your face?
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Get up! Why are you lying face down like this?

L.10: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Rise up! Why [is] this, [that] you are fallen on your face?

R.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Joshua, "Stand up! Why are you lying there with your face on the ground?

decisions.choice: rise up: a sharp command to stop lying on the ground
decisions.reason: The command is followed by "for yourself", a way of making a command firmer and more personal. The question that follows is a rebuke: this is not the time for mourning but for dealing with what has gone wrong (verse 11).

decisions.choice: why is this, that you are fallen: why are you lying there
decisions.reason: "Why this" is an emphatic "why". The participle describes Joshua's present state: he is still lying where he fell in verse 6.

records.heading: Achan is found out

records.source: חָטָא֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְגַם֙ עָבְר֣וּ אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֖יתִי אוֹתָ֑ם וְגַ֤ם לָֽקְחוּ֙ מִן־הַחֵ֔רֶם וְגַ֤ם גָּֽנְבוּ֙ וְגַ֣ם כִּֽחֲשׁ֔וּ וְגַ֖ם שָׂ֥מוּ בִכְלֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Has sinned Israel, and also they have transgressed my covenant which I commanded them; and also they have taken from the devoted thing, and also they have stolen, and also they have deceived, and also they have put [it] among their things.
pieces: Israel has sinned. They have broken {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, which I commanded them to keep. They have taken some of the devoted things. They have stolen, they have lied, and they have put the things among their own belongings.

L.11: Israel has sinned; they have also transgressed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant that I commanded them. They have even taken from the devoted things; they have also stolen, and also deceived, and also put [them] among their own things.

R.11: Israel has sinned. They have broken {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} covenant, the agreement I commanded them to keep. They took some of the devoted things. They stole them and lied about it. They hid them with their own things.

decisions.choice: Israel has sinned: the whole people stands guilty
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks of Israel as one body, as verse 1 does. The guilt of one man rests on the whole people until it is dealt with.

decisions.choice: transgressed my covenant: broke the terms the LORD had laid on them
decisions.reason: "Transgress" means to cross over a line, to break an agreement. The covenant here includes the command about the devoted things at Jericho (6:17-19), given as part of the LORD's covenant with Israel.

decisions.choice: also ... also: a list that grows heavier with each step
decisions.reason: Each charge is introduced by "and also", so the sins pile up: they took what was devoted, they stole it from the LORD, they lied about it, and they hid it with their own goods as if it were theirs.

decisions.choice: deceived: acted falsely, hiding the truth
decisions.reason: The verb means to deny or deceive. Achan went on as if nothing had happened, hiding the theft from Joshua and the people.

decisions.choice: commanded them to keep
decisions.reason: A covenant is not itself commanded; its terms are. Balanced and Readable add "to keep" to make the sense clear.

decisions.choice: the agreement
decisions.reason: Readable explains "covenant" with a plain word once.

records.source: וְלֹ֨א יֻכְל֜וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לָקוּם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אֹיְבֵיהֶ֔ם עֹ֗רֶף יִפְנוּ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אֹֽיְבֵיהֶ֔ם כִּ֥י הָי֖וּ לְחֵ֑רֶם לֹ֤א אוֹסִיף֙ לִֽהְי֣וֹת עִמָּכֶ֔ם אִם־לֹ֥א תַשְׁמִ֛ידוּ הַחֵ֖רֶם מִֽקִּרְבְּכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And not are able [the] sons of Israel to stand before their enemies; [the] back they turn before their enemies, for they have become a devoted thing. Not I will again be with you if not you destroy the devoted thing from your midst.
pieces: That is why the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cannot stand up to their enemies. They turn and run from them, because they themselves have become devoted to destruction. I will not be with you any longer unless you destroy the devoted things that are among you.

L.12: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel are not able to stand before their enemies; they turn [their] back before their enemies, for they have become a devoted thing. I will not be with you again unless you destroy the devoted things from your midst.

R.12: That is why the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} cannot stand up to their enemies. They turn and run away, because now they themselves are under the ban, like the devoted things, set apart for destruction. I will not be with you anymore unless you destroy the devoted things you have among you.

decisions.choice: they have become a devoted thing: Israel itself now falls under the ban
decisions.reason: By taking what was devoted, Israel has brought the ban on itself, as Joshua warned (6:18; Deuteronomy 7:26). It now stands where Jericho stood: given over to destruction. Only by destroying the devoted things can it be freed.

decisions.choice: I will not be with you again: the LORD withdraws the presence he had promised
decisions.reason: The LORD had promised Joshua, "As I was with Moses, I will be with you" (1:5; 3:7). The threat is that this presence, the source of Israel's victories, will end.

decisions.choice: the shift from "they" to "you"
decisions.reason: The verse begins by speaking about Israel and ends by speaking to it (plural "you"). The LORD's words are meant for the people, to be passed on by Joshua (verse 13).

decisions.choice: devoted to destruction
decisions.reason: When the word describes people, as here, Balanced uses "devoted to destruction", the settled rendering of the verb, so that readers see what it means for Israel; the goods themselves stay "devoted things".

decisions.choice: under the ban, like the devoted things, set apart for destruction
decisions.reason: Readable spells out m1: Israel is now in the same position as the devoted things. It keeps the term "devoted things" used in the rest of the chapter.

records.source: קֻ֚ם קַדֵּ֣שׁ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ הִתְקַדְּשׁ֣וּ לְמָחָ֑ר כִּ֣י כֹה֩ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל חֵ֤רֶם בְּקִרְבְּךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹ֣א תוּכַ֗ל לָקוּם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י אֹיְבֶ֔יךָ עַד־הֲסִירְכֶ֥ם הַחֵ֖רֶם מִֽקִּרְבְּכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Rise, consecrate the people and say, Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, for thus says Yahweh, God of Israel: A devoted thing [is] in your midst, Israel; not you will be able to stand before your enemies until you remove the devoted thing from your midst.
pieces: Get up and consecrate the people. Tell them, 'Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: "There are devoted things among you, Israel. You cannot stand up to your enemies until you remove the devoted things from among you."

L.13: Rise, consecrate the people, and say, 'Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow; for thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: "A devoted thing [is] in your midst, Israel; you will not be able to stand before your enemies until you remove the devoted thing from your midst."

R.13: Get up and make the people holy. Tell them, 'Make yourselves holy and get ready for tomorrow. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: "Israel, there are devoted things among you. You will not be able to stand up to your enemies until you get rid of them."

decisions.choice: consecrate: make the people ready to come before the LORD
decisions.reason: To consecrate the people was to make them ready to meet God, usually by washing and keeping themselves clean (Exodus 19:10-15; Joshua 3:5). The next day the LORD himself would point out the guilty one.

decisions.choice: the message Joshua is to give runs from here to the end of verse 15
decisions.reason: The LORD tells Joshua what to say to the people. That message begins here, includes the LORD's own words ("thus says the LORD"), and goes on to the instructions for the next morning in verses 14-15, which speak to the people as "you" (plural).

decisions.choice: a devoted thing: the stolen goods from Jericho, still under the ban
decisions.reason: The singular noun names the devoted goods as a whole, as in verse 1. While they remain in the camp, the whole people is touched by the ban (verse 12).

decisions.choice: make ... holy
decisions.reason: Readable explains "consecrate" with the plainer "make holy", and adds "get ready" for the purpose (m1).

decisions.choice: quotation marks: the LORD's words inside Joshua's message inside the LORD's speech
decisions.reason: The LORD's speech to Joshua (from verse 10) takes double quotation marks; the message Joshua is to give takes single marks; the words "thus says the LORD" introduce a third level, in double marks again, which ends with this verse. The single marks stay open to the end of verse 15 (m2).

records.source: וְנִקְרַבְתֶּ֥ם בַּבֹּ֖קֶר לְשִׁבְטֵיכֶ֑ם וְהָיָ֡ה הַשֵּׁבֶט֩ אֲשֶׁר־יִלְכְּדֶ֨נּוּ יְהוָ֜ה יִקְרַ֣ב לַמִּשְׁפָּח֗וֹת וְהַמִּשְׁפָּחָ֞ה אֲשֶֽׁר־יִלְכְּדֶ֤נָּה יְהוָה֙ תִּקְרַ֣ב לַבָּתִּ֔ים וְהַבַּ֨יִת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִלְכְּדֶ֣נּוּ יְהוָ֔ה יִקְרַ֖ב לַגְּבָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And you will come near in the morning by your tribes; and it will be the tribe which takes it Yahweh will come near by the clans, and the clan which takes it Yahweh will come near by the households, and the household which takes it Yahweh will come near by the men.
pieces: In the morning you are to come forward tribe by tribe. The tribe that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} picks out is to come forward clan by clan. The clan that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} picks out is to come forward household by household, and the household that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} picks out is to come forward man by man.

L.14: And you will be brought near in the morning by your tribes; and it shall be [that] the tribe that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} takes shall come near by clans, and the clan that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} takes shall come near by households, and the household that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} takes shall come near man by man.

R.14: In the morning, come forward one tribe at a time. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will show which tribe it is. Then that tribe will come forward one clan at a time. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will show which clan it is. That clan will come forward one family at a time. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will show which family it is. Then that family will come forward one man at a time.

decisions.choice: takes: selects by lot
decisions.reason: The verb means "capture" or "seize", and is used for choosing someone by lot (1 Samuel 10:20-21; 14:41-42). The text does not say how the lot was cast; it may have been with the Urim and Thummim kept by the priest (Numbers 27:21; 1 Samuel 14:41). Either way, the choice is the LORD's.

decisions.choice: tribes, clans, households, men: the steps of Israel's family structure
decisions.reason: Israel was made up of tribes, each tribe of clans, each clan of households ("father's houses"), each household of its men. The lot narrows the search step by step, as verses 16-18 then show.

decisions.choice: picks out / will show which
decisions.reason: "Take" in the sense of choosing by lot (m1) is put as "picks out" at Balanced and "will show which" at Readable; Literal keeps "takes".

decisions.choice: family
decisions.reason: Readable uses "family" for the household, the group under one head; "clan" stays for the larger group.

records.source: וְהָיָה֙ הַנִּלְכָּ֣ד בַּחֵ֔רֶם יִשָּׂרֵ֣ף בָּאֵ֔שׁ אֹת֖וֹ וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֑וֹ כִּ֤י עָבַר֙ אֶת־בְּרִ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וְכִֽי־עָשָׂ֥ה נְבָלָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And it will be the one taken with the devoted thing will be burned with fire, he and all that [belongs] to him, for he has transgressed [the] covenant of Yahweh and for he has done a disgraceful folly in Israel.
pieces: The one who is picked out with the devoted things is to be burned, he and everything he has, because he has broken the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and has done a shameful thing in Israel.'"

L.15: And it shall be [that] the one taken with the devoted thing shall be burned with fire, he and all that [is] his, because he has transgressed the covenant of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and because he has done an outrageous folly in Israel.'"

R.15: The man who is shown to have the devoted things must be burned with fire, along with everything he owns. He has broken {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s covenant and done a shameful thing in Israel.'"

decisions.choice: burned with fire: the way devoted things were destroyed
decisions.reason: A town or thing devoted to the LORD was burned (6:24; Deuteronomy 13:17). The one who took devoted things has become devoted himself (verse 12), so he and what he has are to be destroyed in the same way. Verse 25 tells how it was carried out.

decisions.choice: all that is his: his possessions, and perhaps his household
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean property only, or all that belonged to a man, including his household. Verse 24 lists his sons and daughters with his animals and tent; see the note there.

decisions.choice: outrageous folly: a shameful act that breaks the bonds of the community
decisions.reason: The word does not mean simple foolishness but a disgraceful act that the community must not tolerate, used of rape and of grave sexual wrong (Genesis 34:7; Deuteronomy 22:21; Judges 20:6). Here it is betraying the LORD and the whole people.

decisions.choice: a shameful thing
decisions.reason: "Folly" sounds mild to modern ears. Balanced and Readable use "shameful" to carry the weight of the word (m3).

records.source: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֤ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וַיַּקְרֵ֥ב אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לִשְׁבָטָ֑יו וַיִּלָּכֵ֖ד שֵׁ֥בֶט יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And rose early Joshua in the morning and brought near Israel by its tribes, and was taken [the] tribe of Judah.
pieces: Joshua rose early the next morning and brought Israel forward by tribes. The tribe of Judah was picked out.

L.16: And Joshua rose early in the morning and brought Israel near by its tribes, and the tribe of Judah was taken.

R.16: Joshua got up early the next morning. He had Israel come forward one tribe at a time, and the tribe of Judah was chosen.

decisions.choice: rose early: Joshua acted at once
decisions.reason: "Rising early" often marks prompt obedience (3:1; 6:12; Genesis 22:3). Joshua does exactly as the LORD said in verse 14.

decisions.choice: was picked out / was chosen
decisions.reason: As in verse 14, "taken" means chosen by lot.

records.source: וַיַּקְרֵב֙ אֶת־מִשְׁפַּ֣חַת יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּלְכֹּ֕ד אֵ֖ת מִשְׁפַּ֣חַת הַזַּרְחִ֑י וַיַּקְרֵ֞ב אֶת־מִשְׁפַּ֤חַת הַזַּרְחִי֙ לַגְּבָרִ֔ים וַיִּלָּכֵ֖ד זַבְדִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And he brought near [the] clan of Judah, and he took [the] clan of the Zerahite; and he brought near [the] clan of the Zerahite by the men, and was taken Zabdi.
pieces: He brought forward the clans of Judah, and the Zerahite clan was picked out. He brought forward the Zerahite clan man by man, and Zabdi was picked out.

L.17: And he brought near the clan of Judah, and he took the clan of the Zerahites; and he brought near the clan of the Zerahites man by man, and Zabdi was taken.

R.17: Next the clans of Judah came forward, and the clan of Zerah was chosen. Then the clan of Zerah came forward man by man, and Zabdi was chosen.

decisions.choice: the clan of Judah: the clans of Judah
alternatives: the clan of Judah (the tribe as a whole)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has the singular "clan of Judah", which would mean the tribe taken as a whole. The Greek translation and a few Hebrew manuscripts have the plural "the clans of Judah", which fits the steps of verse 14. The sense is the same either way: Judah's clans were brought forward in turn.

decisions.choice: man by man: probably household by household
decisions.reason: Verse 14 orders the clan to come forward by households, and Zabdi is the head of a household (verse 18). The Hebrew here reads "by men", perhaps meaning the heads of each household; a few Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac translation read "by households". Either way the household of Zabdi is the one chosen.

decisions.choice: he took: the LORD chose, through the lot
decisions.reason: The subject of "he took" is not named. It is the LORD, who "takes" by the lot (verse 14), though it could be read loosely of Joshua casting it.

decisions.choice: the clan of Zerah
decisions.reason: Readable names the clan by its ancestor rather than as "the Zerahites".

records.source: וַיַּקְרֵ֥ב אֶת־בֵּית֖וֹ לַגְּבָרִ֑ים וַיִּלָּכֵ֗ד עָכָ֞ן בֶּן־כַּרְמִ֧י בֶן־זַבְדִּ֛י בֶּן־זֶ֖רַח לְמַטֵּ֥ה יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he brought near his household by the men, and was taken Achan son of Carmi son of Zabdi son of Zerah, of [the] tribe of Judah.
pieces: He had Zabdi's household come forward man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was picked out.

L.18: And he brought near his household man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken.

R.18: Then he had Zabdi's family come forward one man at a time, and Achan was chosen. He was the son of Carmi and grandson of Zabdi, from the family line of Zerah in the tribe of Judah.

decisions.choice: his household: the household of Zabdi
decisions.reason: "His" points back to Zabdi, the last one named in verse 17. The lot has now narrowed from all Israel to one man, and the full line of descent from verse 1 is repeated to show that the LORD has found the very man.

decisions.choice: Zabdi's household / Zabdi's family
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name whose household is meant (m1). Readable uses "family" for the household, as in verse 14, and explains the line of descent as in verse 1.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ אֶל־עָכָ֗ן בְּנִי֙ שִֽׂים־נָ֣א כָב֗וֹד לַֽיהוָ֛ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְתֶן־ל֣וֹ תוֹדָ֑ה וְהַגֶּד־נָ֥א לִי֙ מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֔יתָ אַל־תְּכַחֵ֖ד מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
records.gloss: And said Joshua to Achan, My son, put please glory to Yahweh, God of Israel, and give to him confession; and tell please to me what you have done; do not hide from me.
pieces: Then Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory now to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel. Make your confession to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Tell me what you have done. Do not hide anything from me."

L.19: And Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory, please, to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, and give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} praise; and tell me, please, what you have done. Do not hide [it] from me."

R.19: Then Joshua said to Achan, "My son, honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, by telling the truth. Confess to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Tell me what you did. Do not hide anything from me."

decisions.choice: give glory to the LORD: honor God by telling the whole truth
decisions.reason: This was a solemn call to speak the truth before God, who already knows it (John 9:24 uses the same words). To confess one's guilt is to admit that God's judgment is right, and so to give him glory.

decisions.choice: praise / confession: the word means both
decisions.reason: The noun means thanks or praise given to God, and also acknowledging something before him. Here it means confessing the wrong (Ezra 10:11 uses it with the same verb for confessing sin). Achan's confession acknowledges that the LORD has judged truly.

decisions.choice: my son: a kind but serious address
decisions.reason: An older man or leader could call a younger one "my son" (1 Samuel 3:6; 2 Samuel 18:22). Joshua speaks gently while asking for a confession that will cost Achan his life.

decisions.choice: make your confession / Confess
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the sense of confessing the wrong (m2). Literal keeps "praise", the word's common meaning, so readers see the link with giving glory.

decisions.choice: honor the LORD ... by telling the truth
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom of giving glory (m1) instead of reproducing it.

records.source: וַיַּ֧עַן עָכָ֛ן אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אָמְנָ֗ה אָנֹכִ֤י חָטָ֨אתִי֙ לַֽיהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְכָזֹ֥את וְכָזֹ֖את עָשִֽׂיתִי׃
records.gloss: And answered Achan Joshua and said, Truly I have sinned against Yahweh, God of Israel, and like this and like this I have done.
pieces: Achan answered Joshua, "It is true. I am the one who sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel. Here is what I did:

L.20: And Achan answered Joshua and said, "Truly, I have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, and thus and thus I have done.

R.20: Achan answered Joshua, "It is true! I have sinned against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel. Here is what I did.

decisions.choice: truly, I have sinned: a full admission
decisions.reason: Achan does not excuse himself. "Truly" stresses that what Joshua suspects is true, and "I" is written out for emphasis: it was he who sinned, and against the LORD himself.

decisions.choice: thus and thus I have done: this is what I did
decisions.reason: The doubled "thus" introduces the full account that follows in verse 21.

records.source: וָאֵ֣רֶא בַשָּׁלָ֡ל אַדֶּ֣רֶת שִׁנְעָר֩ אַחַ֨ת טוֹבָ֜ה וּמָאתַ֧יִם שְׁקָלִ֣ים כֶּ֗סֶף וּלְשׁ֨וֹן זָהָ֤ב אֶחָד֙ חֲמִשִּׁ֤ים שְׁקָלִים֙ מִשְׁקָל֔וֹ וָֽאֶחְמְדֵ֖ם וָֽאֶקָּחֵ֑ם וְהִנָּ֨ם טְמוּנִ֥ים בָּאָ֛רֶץ בְּת֥וֹךְ הָאָֽהֳלִ֖י וְהַכֶּ֥סֶף תַּחְתֶּֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And I saw among the spoil a cloak of Shinar, one, good, and two hundred shekels silver, and a tongue of gold, one, fifty shekels its weight, and I coveted them and took them; and there they [are] hidden in the ground in [the] midst of my tent, and the silver under it.
pieces: Among the spoil I saw a beautiful cloak from Babylonia, {{units:about 5 pounds|200 shekels}} of silver, and a bar of gold weighing {{units:about 1 1/4 pounds|fifty shekels}}. I coveted them and took them, and now they are buried in the ground in the middle of my tent. The silver is at the bottom."

L.21: When I saw among the spoil a fine cloak from Shinar, and 200 shekels of silver, and a tongue of gold, fifty shekels [in] its weight, then I coveted them and took them; and see, they [are] hidden in the ground in the middle of my tent, with the silver under it."

R.21: Among the things we took from Jericho, I saw a beautiful coat from Babylonia, {{units:about 5 pounds|200 shekels}} of silver, and a bar of gold that weighed {{units:about 1 1/4 pounds|fifty shekels}}. I wanted them very much, so I took them. They are buried in the ground in my tent. The silver is at the bottom, under the coat."

decisions.choice: a cloak from Shinar: a costly robe from Babylonia
decisions.reason: Shinar is the old name of the land of Babylon (Genesis 10:10; 11:2). A fine robe from there was a prized imported luxury, the kind of garment worn by kings (Jonah 3:6 uses the same word for a king's robe).

decisions.choice: 200 shekels of silver; a gold bar of fifty shekels: weights, not coins
decisions.reason: There were no coins yet; silver and gold were weighed. A shekel was about two fifths of an ounce, so the silver weighed about 5 pounds and the gold about 1 1/4 pounds. Both belonged to the LORD's treasury (6:19).

decisions.choice: a tongue of gold: a bar or wedge of gold shaped like a tongue
decisions.reason: The word is "tongue", used here for a long, flat piece of gold, a form in which gold was stored or traded.

decisions.choice: I saw ... I coveted ... I took: the path of the sin
decisions.reason: The three verbs trace the sin from seeing to desiring to taking, as with Eve in the garden (Genesis 3:6). "Covet" is the word of the commandment against coveting (Exodus 20:17), and Moses had warned Israel not to covet the silver and gold of the nations' idols nor bring a devoted thing into their homes (Deuteronomy 7:25-26).

decisions.choice: under it: under the cloak
decisions.reason: "It" is feminine, matching the word for the cloak, not the word for tent. The cloak was laid over the silver in the hole.

decisions.choice: about 5 pounds / about 1 1/4 pounds
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give modern weights, with the shekels as the reader's alternative; Literal keeps the shekels.

decisions.choice: Babylonia; a bar of gold
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the land's familiar name and the plain word for the shape (m1, m3). Literal keeps "Shinar" and "tongue".

decisions.choice: the things we took from Jericho
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the spoil" as the goods taken at Jericho, all of which were devoted to the LORD.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים וַיָּרֻ֖צוּ הָאֹ֑הֱלָה וְהִנֵּ֧ה טְמוּנָ֛ה בְּאָהֳל֖וֹ וְהַכֶּ֥סֶף תַּחְתֶּֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And sent Joshua messengers, and they ran to the tent; and there, [it was] hidden in his tent, and the silver under it.
pieces: So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. There it was, hidden in his tent, with the silver underneath.

L.22: And Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent; and look, [it was] hidden in his tent, with the silver under it.

R.22: So Joshua sent some men, and they ran to Achan's tent. The things were there, hidden in his tent, with the silver at the bottom.

decisions.choice: there, hidden: what they found matched Achan's words
decisions.reason: "Look" turns the reader's eyes to what the messengers saw. "Hidden" is feminine singular, matching the cloak, the item on top; everything was just as Achan had said (verse 21).

decisions.choice: Achan's tent / The things
decisions.reason: Readable names whose tent it was and what was found.

records.source: וַיִּקָּחוּם֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הָאֹ֔הֶל וַיְבִאוּם֙ אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ וְאֶ֖ל כָּל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיַּצִּקֻ֖ם לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they took them from [the] midst of the tent and brought them to Joshua and to all [the] sons of Israel, and they poured them out before Yahweh.
pieces: They took the things out of the tent, brought them to Joshua and all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and laid them out before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.23: And they took them from the middle of the tent and brought them to Joshua and to all the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and they poured them out before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.23: They took the things out of the tent and brought them to Joshua and all the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. Then they spread them out on the ground in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: poured them out before the LORD: laid them out in the LORD's presence
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to pour. Here the goods are spread out on the ground for all to see, before the ark (verse 6). What was stolen from the LORD is handed back to him.

decisions.choice: laid them out / spread them out
decisions.reason: "Poured" would suggest a liquid; Balanced and Readable say what was done with the goods (m1).

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֣ח יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ אֶת־עָכָ֣ן בֶּן־זֶ֡רַח וְאֶת־הַכֶּ֣סֶף וְאֶת־הָאַדֶּ֣רֶת וְֽאֶת־לְשׁ֣וֹן הַזָּהָ֡ב וְֽאֶת־בָּנָ֡יו וְֽאֶת־בְּנֹתָ֡יו וְאֶת־שׁוֹרוֹ֩ וְאֶת־חֲמֹר֨וֹ וְאֶת־צֹאנ֤וֹ וְאֶֽת־אָהֳלוֹ֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֔וֹ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עִמּ֑וֹ וַיַּעֲל֥וּ אֹתָ֖ם עֵ֥מֶק עָכֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: And took Joshua Achan son of Zerah and the silver and the cloak and [the] tongue of the gold and his sons and his daughters and his ox and his donkey and his flock and his tent and all that [belonged] to him, and all Israel with him, and they brought them up [to the] valley of Achor.
pieces: Then Joshua, and all Israel with him, seized Achan son of Zerah, together with the silver, the cloak and the gold bar, his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys and sheep, his tent, and all that he owned, and they led them up to the Valley of Achor.

L.24: And Joshua took Achan son of Zerah, and the silver and the cloak and the tongue of gold, and his sons and his daughters, and his oxen and his donkeys and his flock, and his tent, and all that [was] his, and all Israel with him; and they brought them up [to the] Valley of Achor.

R.24: Then Joshua and all the people of Israel took Achan, a descendant of Zerah. They took the silver, the coat and the bar of gold. They also took his sons and daughters, his cattle, donkeys and sheep, his tent, and everything else he owned. They brought them all to the Valley of Achor.

decisions.choice: Achan son of Zerah: a descendant of Zerah
decisions.reason: Zerah was Achan's distant ancestor (verse 1); "son" here means descendant.

decisions.choice: his sons and his daughters: whether they shared his punishment
alternatives: the family was put to death with Achan
the family was brought to watch the judgment
decisions.reason: The family is brought out with the animals and goods, and verse 25 says "they burned them" and "stoned them". This may mean the household died with Achan, as when a whole household was destroyed with its head (Numbers 16:27-33); hiding the goods in the family tent may have made them party to the crime. Others read the family as brought only to witness, since the Law forbids putting children to death for a father's sin (Deuteronomy 24:16), and take "them" in verse 25 to mean Achan's goods and animals. The text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: his ox, his donkey, his flock: all his animals
decisions.reason: The singular nouns stand for whole kinds of animal: his cattle, his donkeys and his sheep and goats. Everything Achan owned is treated as devoted (verse 15).

decisions.choice: the Valley of Achor: a valley leading up from the Jordan plain
decisions.reason: The valley lay on the edge of the land near Jericho; it later marked the border of Judah (15:7). Its name is explained in verse 26.

decisions.choice: cattle / sheep
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plural or group words for the animals (m3). "Flock" can mean sheep and goats; "sheep" is used as the common word.

decisions.choice: Then Joshua, and all Israel with him, seized ...
decisions.reason: Balanced moves "and all Israel with him" next to Joshua, the subject, so the long list does not separate them.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֨עַ֙ מֶ֣ה עֲכַרְתָּ֔נוּ יַעְכֳּרְךָ֥ יְהוָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וַיִּרְגְּמ֨וּ אֹת֤וֹ כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶ֔בֶן וַיִּשְׂרְפ֤וּ אֹתָם֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ וַיִּסְקְל֥וּ אֹתָ֖ם בָּאֲבָנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And said Joshua, Why have you troubled us? Will trouble you Yahweh on this day. And stoned him all Israel [with] stone, and they burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.
pieces: Joshua said, "Why have you brought trouble on us? {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will bring trouble on you today." Then all Israel stoned him; they burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.

L.25: And Joshua said, "Why have you troubled us? {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will trouble you this day." And all Israel stoned him with stones; and they burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.

R.25: Joshua said, "Why have you brought all this trouble on us? Now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will bring trouble on you today." Then all the people of Israel threw stones at Achan until he died. They burned them with fire and also threw stones at them.

decisions.choice: trouble: the word that gives the valley its name
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring disaster on someone, to stir up trouble. It sounds like the names Achan and Achor. Joshua had warned that taking devoted things would "trouble" the camp (6:18); now the one who troubled Israel is troubled in turn. See verse 26.

decisions.choice: him ... them: Achan, and those or what was taken with him
decisions.reason: "Him" is Achan. The plural "them" may mean his household, or his goods and animals together with his body; on the question of the family, see verse 24. Two different verbs for stoning are used, the second with the plural, so the stones may have been heaped over the burned remains as well.

decisions.choice: stoned and burned: execution by the whole people, then destruction by fire
decisions.reason: Stoning was carried out by the community together (Leviticus 24:14; Deuteronomy 13:10-11). Burning followed the command for one taken with the devoted things (verse 15).

decisions.choice: until he died
decisions.reason: Readable says that the stoning of Achan was an execution. It keeps the plural "them" in the next sentence, which leaves open who or what they were, as the Hebrew does (m2).

decisions.choice: brought trouble on
decisions.reason: "Troubled" sounds like mild worry in modern English; the verb means to bring disaster.

records.source: וַיָּקִ֨ימוּ עָלָ֜יו גַּל־אֲבָנִ֣ים גָּד֗וֹל עַ֚ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה וַיָּ֥שָׁב יְהוָ֖ה מֵחֲר֣וֹן אַפּ֑וֹ עַל־כֵּ֠ן קָרָ֞א שֵׁ֣ם הַמָּק֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ עֵ֣מֶק עָכ֔וֹר עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And they raised over him a heap of stones, great, until this day; and turned Yahweh from [the] burning of his anger. Therefore one called [the] name of that place Valley of Achor until this day.
pieces: They raised a large pile of stones over him, which is there to this day. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} turned from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} burning anger. That is why the place has been called the Valley of Achor ever since.

L.26: And they raised over him a great heap of stones, [which is there] until this day; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} turned from the burning of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger. Therefore the name of that place has been called [the] Valley of Achor until this day.

R.26: They piled a big heap of stones over Achan, and it is still there today. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was no longer angry. That is why the place is still called the Valley of Achor, which means Valley of Trouble.

decisions.choice: Valley of Achor: the name means "valley of trouble"
decisions.reason: Achor comes from the same root as the verb "trouble" in verse 25, so the place name recalls what happened there: Achan troubled Israel and was himself troubled. 1 Chronicles 2:7 even calls him Achar, "the troubler of Israel". The prophets later promise that this valley of trouble will become a place of rest and a door of hope (Isaiah 65:10; Hosea 2:17).

decisions.choice: a heap of stones until this day: a memorial still seen when the book was written
decisions.reason: Heaps of stones marked places where something important had happened (4:9; 8:29; Genesis 31:46-48). "Until this day" means the heap could still be seen in the writer's time. This heap stands in contrast to the memorial stones of the Jordan crossing (4:9).

decisions.choice: the LORD turned from his burning anger: the wrath of verse 1 is ended
decisions.reason: The chapter opens with the LORD's anger burning against Israel and closes with it turned away, once the devoted things were removed (verses 12-13). The way is open for victory at Ai (8:1).

decisions.choice: one called: the place came to be called
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; it means the place was given this name, and the name stuck.

decisions.choice: which means Valley of Trouble
decisions.reason: Readable adds the meaning of the name, since the point of the verse is the wordplay (m1). Literal and Balanced keep the name and leave the meaning to the note.

decisions.choice: was no longer angry
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "turned from his burning anger" means.
